name: Upper Limb Mesomelic Dysplasia, Type Fryns
aliases: Fryns Type Upper Limb Mesomelic Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Fryns Type Upper Limb Mesomelic Dysplasia Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Mesomelic shortening of the upper limbs characterized by shortening of the forearm bones (radius and ulna)
Radioulnar synostosis or fusion of the radius and ulna bones
Normal or minimally affected lower limbs differentiating from other mesomelic dysplasias
Mild facial dysmorphic features such as midface hypoplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of mesomelic shortening of the upper limbs with radioulnar synostosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may assist but causative gene not definitively identified.

imaging: Radiographs showing mesomelic shortening of radius and ulna
Radioulnar synostosis or fusion on X-ray
genetic: No definitive causative gene identified; genetic heterogeneity suspected
other: Clinical examination revealing limited forearm rotation

distinguishingFeatures: Involvement of both upper and lower limbs
Severe mesomelic shortening affecting all limbs

redFlags: Associated respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage abnormalities
references: Fryns JP, et al. Upper limb mesomelic dysplasia: clinical and radiological features. Am J Med Genet. 1990.
Orphanet: Upper limb mesomelic dysplasia, type Fryns - ORPHA:2497
Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019.
